tagline: Break bonds, not the fuel: engineered biodesulfurization as a polishing step for refractory sulfur in diesel.
summary: Nulfur rebuilds the four-enzyme 4S biodesulfurization pathway (DszA, DszB, DszC plus a flavin reductase) from Rhodococcus erythropolis inside Pseudomonas putida KT2440, targeting dibenzothiophene (DBT) — the refractory sulfur compound that conventional hydrodesulfurization struggles to remove without running at 300-400 C and 3-6 MPa. Rather than replacing hydrodesulfurization, the team reframed the project after industry consultation as a modular side-stream polishing step on diesel. The project won on the strength of its alternative chassis work: because P. putida is a non-model organism, the team built the missing toolkit from scratch (a Golden Gate-compatible broad-host-range vector, a measured four-promoter set, and a working heat-shock transformation protocol) and published it as a handbook for other teams. That platform contribution, paired with an unusually deep dry lab (COBRApy genome-scale modelling, a FoldX/ThermoMPNN protein engineering pipeline, and an agentic AI research platform called Cofactor), won Best Alternative Platform and Best Wiki and Best Bioremediation Project nominations.

dry.frameworks: Three distinct computational layers. (1) Genome-scale metabolic modelling: the published P. putida KT2440 model iJN1463 was extended in COBRApy with the heterologous 4S pathway reactions (DszA/B/C/D), and flux balance analysis solved through GLPK over a 1000-point sweep of the DBT exchange flux bound showed metabolism never bottlenecks uptake, while forcing DszB flux revealed an NADH-limited ceiling of 9.80 mmol gDCW-1 h-1 that formate co-feeding raises 25.5% to 12.30. (2) A first-principles mass-transfer model of the biphasic reactor combining Hinze-Kolmogorov droplet-breakup scaling, film theory at the stagnant-sphere limit (Sh = 2), micellar solubilization above the CMC and Michaelis-Menten uptake, solved by bisection for the steady-state free DBT concentration; it predicts rhamnolipid raises effective DBT availability 2.8- to 34-fold. (3) A protein engineering pipeline that screened over 1,100 candidate substitutions in DszB and DszC using ConSurf conservation grades, MD-derived backbone RMSF, and an ensemble of FoldX (empirical force field) plus ThermoMPNN (deep learning on ProteinMPNN embeddings) for ddG, then validated catalytic integrity with explicit-solvent GROMACS MD (amber99sb-ildn, TIP3P) and AutoDock Vina ligand docking before shortlisting five mutants per enzyme.
dry.dataviz: The wiki is a server-rendered-feel React site with a genuinely engineered visual layer: a WebGL/Three.js distillation-tower scene and animated pathway loop on the landing page, every equation rendered as its own labelled SVG so the derivation reads as a chain, and predictor-agreement scatter plots (Figure 9) that shade the quadrant where FoldX and ThermoMPNN both call a substitution stabilising and enlarge it to label the five mutations actually sent to the bench. The Human Practices page is built as a clickable stacked column where each band is one of seven kinds of conversation across 21 entries, so a judge can jump straight to the stakeholder group they care about. Every figure carries a long descriptive alt attribute that states the figure's actual numbers, not just its subject.
dry.datascience: The headline data-science contribution is turning the protein engineering loop into a measured, auditable artefact. The team built a six-arm evaluation suite for Cofactor with four ablation regimes (bare, bare_prompt, tools, full) that add exactly one harness layer each, then scored outcomes: 37 deterministic probes in Arms A and B all pass, Arm C recorded zero workflow violations across 27 scorable runs under the phase machine versus two in the bare condition, and Arm D found the ungrounded condition hallucinated amino-acid positions while both grounded conditions did not. Arm E asked the agent to reconstruct the initial experimental designs of six published papers (three postdating the model's knowledge cutoff) and audited tool transcripts for contamination. On the wet-lab side, the promoter library was quantified as log-normalized mScarlet-i fluorescence per OD600 corrected for media background and P. putida autofluorescence, which revealed only three distinct expression tiers rather than the four reported in the literature.
dry.software: Cofactor, an agentic protein engineering platform released under MIT licence at https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/uottawa/cofactor. It wraps a general-purpose LLM in an explicit phase state machine whose preconditions are checked against a 16-table SQLite store (.cofactor/research.sqlite3, WAL journaling, foreign keys) rather than against the model's claims, so runs resume across sessions and the research record stays readable without the tool. A deterministic tool layer covers sequence operations, RFC10 compliance checking, codon optimisation, restriction analysis, solubility scanning, and retrieval from UniProt, NCBI, RCSB PDB, AlphaFold, PubMed and Europe PMC; an ExecutionManager submits jobs to local, SSH or Slurm backends. Three frontends ship: a FastAPI web UI, a Textual TUI and a CLI, all bring-your-own-key and model-agnostic against any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The team also released the P. putida handbook with protocols and the sanitized Golden Gate-ready pBBR1MCS-2 vector to the iGEM Registry.

good.publicEngagement: Education is organised around four stated principles - Access, Adapt, Engage, Extend - and each initiative is written up against one of them. The team ran bilingual (English/French) sessions for 370+ children aged 4-13 in the Ottawa-Carleton District School Board's International and Indigenous Languages Program summer school, reached 70 more through the Ottawa Catholic School Board, and visited AcadeCap International School for ages 4-7. Original hands-on activities include Lava Lamps (oil properties), The Art of Consortia (a collaborative mural standing in for microbial division of labour), Mix and Match Genes, The Power of Bacterial DNA, and a Heavy vs Light Oil worksheet. For durability they published a free interactive children's magazine, Bio-Builder, distributed through local Ottawa public libraries explicitly to reach low-income families who cannot buy such resources, plus a demo list, infographics, a science and research podcast, and a full downloadable resource library of presentations and worksheets so the activities run without the team present. They also hosted the Great Canadian iGEM Incubator poster competition (with QGEM) and the Great Canadian Meetup pitch competition, both with published scoring rubrics.
good.ihp: 21 conversations across seven categories, each logged in the same three-part structure: why we went, what we heard, what we changed. The changes are concrete. Dr. Jinwen Chen (Natural Resources Canada, CanmetENERGY-Devon) and Dr. Stephen Larter (Calgary, petroleum geochemist) both told the team to abandon heavy diluted bitumen for diesel because of viscosity, mass-transfer and emulsion-separation barriers, and because diesel carries a hard <10 ppm sulfur limit and concentrated refractory DBTs - the team moved its entire target stream to diesel polishing. Dr. Rasha Maal-Bared warned that viscous crude mixes in localised laminar flow, which put static mixing elements and bioreactor sizing into the continuous-flow design. Patrick Lumley (Safe Sulphur Systems, 33 years in sulfur recovery) said the aqueous sulfite byproduct needs pH control to prevent SO2 release and that Claus-plant load reduction is economically worthless - so a pH control loop went into the P&ID and the business case was rebuilt around hydrogen savings and reduced hydrotreating severity instead of sulfur throughput. Larter's warning about microbially influenced corrosion added corrosion and material-compatibility criteria to the reactor design. Faculty of Engineering Design Day feedback forced the pivot from a full HDS-replacement narrative to the complementary polishing model. Dr. Corrie DaCosta, a protein chemist, was consulted specifically about what Cofactor's output report must contain to be usable by the person doing the engineering, and the report format changed as a result.
good.realWorld: A fully worked commercialization case. Market sizing: TAM ~$3.1B (global HDS catalyst market), SAM ~$66M (Canada's 2.2% share, 16 refineries, ~2M bbl/day), SOM ~$1.4M from a single-refinery side-stream demo at a $0.40/bbl royalty on a 10,000 bbl/day stream. Revenue model is per-barrel licensing royalties, validated in conversation with an operations and project engineer. A techno-economic analysis compares BDS against HDS CAPEX of $16-42M USD for a 20,000-25,000 bbl/day refinery and projects 50-60% CAPEX reduction from eliminating high-pressure hydrogen hardware; a life cycle assessment with a declared system boundary and BDS/HDS inventories backs the environmental claim rather than asserting it. A staged timeline runs from proof of concept (2026) through publication and NSERC Alliance / Mitacs Accelerate / CRIN non-dilutive funding (2027), pilot demonstration on real feedstock plus formal pre-engagement with Environment and Climate Change Canada under New Substances Notification regulations for contained LMO deployment (2028-29), to licensing (2030+) and expansion into biodenitrogenation. The team deliberately targets smaller, older refineries facing Euro V limits with constrained hydrogen capacity rather than major oil sands operators, on Lumley's advice, and flags biogas producers as a faster early-revenue path. Risk analysis, SWOT, Business Model Canvas and a competitive positioning matrix are all published, and the team is explicit that Nulfur is harm reduction during the energy transition - "a bridge, not a destination".

gemsTakeaway: Copy uOttawa's human-practices template literally: a single page where every one of 21 stakeholder conversations is logged in the same three fields - why we went, what we heard, what we changed - with the change written as a specific design edit (a pH loop in the P&ID, a switch of feedstock, static mixers). It costs nothing to adopt, makes a student team's reasoning auditable, and is the clearest way a school research centre can show that outside input actually moved the project rather than decorating it.
